name: PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk

frontmatter.title: Chandra Asri: the nine-month spread reset turns the buyback story into a margin story
frontmatter.summary: Revision after review: the base margin was rebuilt from the independent half and quarter spreads, not the nine-month average that contains the clean first half. The spread reset, not the profit base effect, now drives the call, and the price sits far above our fundamental value; Cycle & Carriage is carried as a wash. We move to REDUCE at Rp1,101.
thesis: The headline decline is a base effect: the prior-year nine months carried a US$1,812.2m bargain-purchase gain that is nil this year, while revenue rose to US$8,189.2m; but the third quarter was loss-making at the operating line and needed other gains to hold the nine-month total positive [S17, S16].

The operating news is the third quarter: the nine-month gross margin is well below the first half because Q3 alone fell to a thin margin, and the finished-goods allowance is unchanged at US$62.6m, so this is spread, not write-down [S17, S2].

We set the base margin at 13.4% at the anchor from the independent H1 and Q3 observations, not the nine-month average, and rebuild FY2026E from the nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter at the Q3 run-rate; the DCF equity value floors at Rp0 and the probability-weighted twelve-month fundamental is Rp319 [S17, S2, S0].

The balance sheet is rolled to 30 September: cash US$2,962.7m, financing liabilities US$6,093.9m, associates US$211.0m and current financial assets US$300.0m, and the bridge carries a Q3 cash-flow correction [S17].

The buyback is close to neutral at today's price but transfers value at the ceiling: up to IDR2.00tn for 1,600m shares to January 2027 at no more than Rp3,000, treasury stock with the count held flat [S13, S14, S12, S0].

At Rp1,350 the stock is 4.86 times today's fundamental; the lens keeps part of that premium only because a thin register and a buyback bid slow the close, and it still gives -18.4%, so we move to REDUCE [S0].

catalysts.event: First contribution from the Cycle & Carriage automotive distribution acquisition, completed 15 October 2026, in the fourth-quarter results
End of the buyback period; executed volume and the treasury balance
CA-EDC chlor-alkali and EDC plant scheduled start-up in Q1 2027; the audited FY2026 annual report follows the statutory cycle
MSCI consultation feedback closes; decision on Standalone status due mid-2027

blocks.text: What changed and why. This revision answers the review of the 30 October update (version five). The base gross margin was not the midpoint we called it: the "nine-month trough" was the nine-month average, which contains the clean first half, so the two brackets overlapped and the forecast implied a fourth-quarter recovery after a near-zero third quarter. We rebuilt the base margin from the two independent observations, the clean half and the quarter alone, and rebuilt FY2026E from the nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter at the third-quarter spread; the value falls and the rating moves to REDUCE at a target of Rp1,101 [S17, S2, S0]. Chandra Asri filed its nine-month accounts on 30 October 2026 with revenue of US$8,189.2m and attributable profit of US$279.8m; the decline is a base effect, because the prior-year nine months carried a US$1,812.2m bargain-purchase gain on Aster that this year has none [S17, S16]. The operating news is worse: the third quarter alone earned a thin gross margin and, after depreciation, selling, administration and final tax, its operating EBITDA, profit before tax and attributable profit were all negative, rescued only by other gains; the finished-goods allowance is unchanged at US$62.6m, so this is spread, not write-down [S17, S2].

The release adds two things. Reported nine-month EBITDA was US$981.0m at a 12.0% margin, struck on the US$710.2m segment result, so it is a cross-check, not our operating EBITDA [S18, S17]. Cycle & Carriage completed on 15 October 2026; management guides to a fourth-quarter contribution and group revenue toward US$15,000.0m, but with no consideration or acquired earnings disclosed we carry it as an explicit wash — consideration assumed equal to the net present value of the acquired earnings — and give it value only in the bull [S18, S17]. Funding for it, CA-EDC Phase II and the 2027 maturities is not disclosed; our search found no rights issue or placement in preparation, the current-debt wall is covered about three times by cash, and a placement is a low-to-moderate probability with a proportionate per-share cost [S17, S18, F80-F83].

The target walk. We set the base margin at 13.4% at base input costs, the top of the independent clean-half and third-quarter range; lift the forward tax rate; rebuild working capital; restate the balance sheet to 30 September; and add the Q3 cash-flow correction. The DCF equity value floors at Rp0: at these spreads the discounted operating value barely covers net debt and the minority, and the positive part of the probability-weighted fundamental of Rp319 comes from the bull spread case [S17, S0]. The konglo lens keeps part of the premium because the register is thin and a buyback bid is in place, and lands the target at Rp1,101, a -18.4% return and an REDUCE [S0].

The buyback and the variant view. The company replaced its earlier programme on 28 October 2026 with up to IDR2.00tn for 1,600m shares at a maximum of Rp3,000 to 28 January 2027 [S13, S14, S12]. Treasury stock is an asset and execution is discretionary, so the count is flat; the purchase is neutral only at fundamental value, and today's price is above it [S14, S0]. What changes the view is a sustained spread recovery and an on-time CA-EDC start, not a buyback [S0, S17, S5].

Chandra Asri Pacific is the listed chemicals and energy arm of the Barito Pacific group, controlled by Prajogo Pangestu [S2]. Its infrastructure arm is the separately listed PT Chandra Daya Investasi, 60 per cent owned [S5, S2]. The group reports three segments: Energy & Chemicals, Integrated Infrastructure and Mobility Solutions [S17].

Chemicals is the original naphtha cracker and polyolefins business. Aster adds refinery products and petrochemicals and is why revenue multiplied; Aster Polymer Solutions adds 400 ktpa of HDPE capacity [S4, S5]. CDIA runs power, water, port, storage and logistics [S5, S2]. Cycle & Carriage adds automotive distribution in Singapore and Malaysia, carried as a wash and given value only in the bull [S17, S18]. The growth story is CA-EDC, a US$800.0m chlor-alkali and EDC project at 80.0% construction progress, scheduled for the first quarter of 2027, with US$200.0m of Danantara and INA funding and a planned 400,000-tonne caustic soda capacity [S5, S18]. The first full year of output is the step from the 3.0% baseline to 5.0%, inside the DCF [S5, S17]. Phase II, at about the same size, is pre-FID and excluded — the most likely treatment, not a zero valuation of Phase I [S6].

The realised numbers show a downcycle: the third quarter alone earned a thin gross margin, down from the mid-teens in the clean first half, with the inventory allowance unchanged, so the marginal producer's cash cost is again setting the price [S17]. We value on a through-cycle spread and treat the oil tape as a timing input [S0].

The cost curve runs through oil. The house deck has Brent at 96 for FY2026E, 84 for FY2027E and a long-run anchor of 75, against a FY2025 average of 68; spot is 113 [S0]. The path raises feedstock cost and, with partial pass-through, squeezes the spread; the third quarter shows the squeeze can far exceed the linear link [S17, S0]. We carry the cost side and a mid-cycle marker, with no unsourced crack credit [S17, S2].

Competitive position rests on integration and scale, not cost leadership: the refinery gives feedstock flexibility and the cracker local access, but neither is durable against a Middle East gas-based producer. We place the complex mid-curve, not first quartile, as a judgment: the LK has no cost-curve data [S17]. The forces read badly on commodity polymers and better in EDC and caustic, where the domestic alternative is an import [S5].

The history is a trough. FY2025 is the transformation year, revenue US$7,000.0m with Aster consolidated from mid-year, but EBITDA US$-389.2m because the refinery ran at a trough spread: the prior-year comparative shows revenue US$5,102.4m against raw materials and manufacturing US$5,135.5m, a gross loss [S0, S17]. Those lines are pack-derived and not retrievable audited, so we mark the last audited year unverified [S0, S5]. The nine months to September 2026 are the last actual: revenue US$8,189.2m, raw materials and manufacturing US$7,229.3m, profit before tax US$409.1m, tax US$14.1m and attributable profit US$279.8m [S17].

The company's own release. Reported nine-month EBITDA was US$981.0m at a 12.0% margin, above the LK's US$710.2m total segment result, so it is a cross-check; Energy & Chemicals carried US$604.0m of that result, Integrated Infrastructure US$2.5m and Mobility Solutions US$103.7m [S18, S17]. Cycle & Carriage closed after the period and is excluded [S18].

Our forecast. FY2026E revenue grows 57.6% to US$11,032.0m; FY2027E grows 5.0% as CA-EDC delivers its first full year, then 3.0% volume growth [S17, S5]. The 13.4% base-input margin sits at the top of the independent H1-2026 and Q3-2026 range, grossed back through the oil link to the FY2025 Brent anchor: H1 is the only clean full half and Q3 alone is the cyclical trough, so we take the top of that independent pair; repricing gives 9.1% in FY2026E and 11.0% in FY2027E as Brent falls [S17, S2, S0]. The forward tax rate starts at the nine-month effective 3.5% and steps to 15.0% by FY2030E [S17].

Costs. The opex ratio reconciles to the LK at 6.3% of revenue, including depreciation, selling, G&A, final tax and a recurring other-net charge; the third-quarter gain is excluded [S17]. The Brent link calibrates 60.0% of the cost base as oil-linked with 80.0% pass-through [S17, S2].

Cash flow and capex. Nine-month PP&E acquisitions were US$572.5m against operating cash flow of US$378.9m: the operating business did not fund capex, and cash flow was negative before the inventory release [S17, S2]. Capex is forecast at 6.9% of revenue in FY2026E while CA-EDC completes, then 5.5% and 4.5% [S17, S5]. Working capital is 9.9% of revenue at the 30 September actual — receivables US$985.5m plus inventories US$1,761.3m, less payables US$1,678.6m — a released ratio; from FY2027E we rebuild it to the H1 12.8% [S17, S2]. FY2026E free cash flow to the firm is US$-667.4m [S17].

Balance sheet and debt. The forecast rolls from the 30 September 2026 LK: cash US$2,962.7m, financing liabilities US$6,093.9m, associates US$211.0m and other current financial assets US$300.0m [S17]. The debt wall inside twelve months is US$402.0m of short-term bank loans, US$205.7m of current bank maturities, US$250.9m of current bonds and US$76.2m of current leases; cash of US$2,962.7m covers the total, so the 2027 maturities are a refinancing task rather than an immediate liquidity event [S17, F80-F83]. FY2026E net debt is US$3,635.5m at 5.6x EBITDA, easing to US$4,093.0m at 4.6x [S0]. Interest cover is thin, the bear takes equity value to zero, and no covenant headroom is disclosed [S0, S17].

Capital allocation and quality. The company pays a small dividend, US$30.0m at the parent in the half [S2, S0]. The IDR2.00tn buyback to January 2027 for 1,600m shares at Rp3,000 is treasury stock with discretionary execution, so the count is flat; excluding both the cash out and the treasury accretion overstates per-share value above fundamental value, an error that runs against our REDUCE [S13, S14, S12, S0]. The nine-month accruals ratio is close to zero — net profit of US$394.9m against operating cash flow of US$378.9m on total assets of US$14,220.4m [S17]; the FY2025 comparison is distorted by the US$1,772.2m non-cash bargain gain [S2, S0]. Related-party sales were 1.9% of revenue, and the shares are on the main board with no special notation [S2, S0].

We value TPIA on a through-cycle FCFF DCF; forward EV/EBITDA and PE are cross-checks. We weight the DCF fully because the multiple legs run on trailing pack metrics — FY2025A EBITDA of US$-389.2m is negative and parent earnings of US$1,090.1m carry the US$1,772.2m bargain gain — so the multiples are a cycle check only [S0, S2].

The cost of capital uses the house deck and config inputs: risk-free 4.9%, equity risk premium plus country risk of 4.2% and 2.5%, a levered beta of 1.56, and pre-tax debt cost of 6.9%, giving cost of equity of 15.4% and WACC of 10.5%.

The DCF produces Rp0 a share and an enterprise value of US$3,273.6mm, with terminal value 55.5% of the total [S0]. The reset is the margin, tax and working-capital corrections, not a higher top line [S17, S0]. Cycle & Carriage is not in the bridge because with no consideration or acquired earnings disclosed it cannot be marked; the wash and its bull-only contribution are stated above [S18, S17].

The CDIA marks, and the rule. The base DCF carries the 60 per cent of CDIA TPIA owns at fundamental value, and the bridge separately marks the minority. At CDIA's current lens fundamental the minority sits about a third below its 30 September book value of US$473.9m, so the bridge adds back the difference; at the house target or market price the minority exceeds book and the bridge deducts [S15, F85]. The rule is fundamental, not house-target, because the parent's konglo lens is applied once at TPIA level [S15, S0].

Cycle position and the oil NAV. Spot Brent is 113 against a long-run anchor of 75; the deck's path stays above the anchor in every forecast year (FY2029E 78 against 75), so the DCF is struck on the market path, above the through-cycle marker [S0]. That is the conservative end: a higher Brent raises feedstock cost and, with partial pass-through, lowers the margin and value, so a flat-anchor re-strike would be worth more, not less. We can bound it: the path sits about ten dollars above the anchor, so at the calibrated tenth of a point of gross margin per dollar the anchor margin is about one point higher; the sensitivity grid's one-point higher gross-margin cell at base revenue growth is just over three hundred rupiah a share, and the weighted figure rises through the bull, but the lens target stays far below the Rp1,350 price, so the anchor NAV cannot restore the REDUCE [S0, S17]. At spot with no reversion the value is zero because the debt does not de-lever at a trough spread [S0, S17]. The price discounts both a spread recovery and a re-rating the accounts do not yet support, not our anchor [S0].

The cross-checks, reconciled. The shares trade at 17.2x FY2026E and 13.0x FY2027E EV/EBITDA, and at 129.6x and 40.4x PE [S0]. At the peer-median EV/EBITDA the FY2026E check implies about a third of our twelve-month fundamental, because that EBITDA carries a near-zero fourth quarter; the FY2027E check is a genuine counter-signal, implying a value about a quarter above our fundamental, because the multiple capitalises pre-D&A EBITDA while our FCFF is still negative after the capex and working-capital rebuild. The PE check is below the fundamental on both years because earnings are small and heavily depreciated. Neither multiple approaches the Rp1,350 price: the gap is the spread recovery the market prices and we do not, and the stock trades at a large premium to the peer median [S0].

The sensitivity grid moves gross margin either side of the base and WACC by a like amount; the gross-margin leg dominates [S0]. No public Asian spread index exists in our archive, so the marker is the top of the independent clean-half and third-quarter range, and we show the range [S17, S0].

What the price implies. The engine's reverse DCF cannot bracket the Rp1,350 price because the base business value floors at zero, so we do not quote an implied growth rate; the price therefore pays for a spread recovery well beyond the 13.4% base margin, not for a growth rate the asset base can support, since FY2027E revenue growth is 5.0% and the long-run rate is 3.0% [S0, S17].

The konglo lens. Price is 4.86 times our fundamental value today of Rp277.8 [S0]. The regime targets are Rp512 in the bear case, Rp964 in the base case (closing 30.0%) and Rp1,963 in the bull case; weighting the regime cases a quarter bear, a half base and a quarter bull, the probability-weighted target is Rp1,101, a -18.4% return [S0]. The float is 25.4% and the controller holds 74.5%, so a thin register sets the marginal price; the IDR2.00tn buyback is large against average daily value of IDR395.1bn but runs only to 28 January 2027 [S0, S2, S13]. The May 2026 MSCI deletion removed index buyers and the Standalone decision due by June 2027 caps any re-rating [S10, S9, S0, S13].

The business scenarios are mirrored gross-margin shocks, with no revenue-growth shock, because capacity and capex are fixed [S0, S5]. The base carries 45% of the probability, the bear 35% and the bull 20%, so the high-likelihood spread risk is reflected in the weights [S0]. The payoff is convex and floored: the bull twelve-month value is Rp1,594, while the base and bear both floor at zero because debt and the minority sit ahead of equity — the base's un-floored equity is negative by only about fifteen rupiah a share, a small fraction of the price, and the bear's by about the whole share price — so neither adds to the Rp319 weighted value, which is entirely the bull [S0].

The konglo lens, stated plainly. The Rp1,350 price is 4.86 times today's fundamental of Rp277.8; the base regime closes 30.0% of the log premium and keeps the rest, putting the base-regime target at Rp964, above the twelve-month fundamental of Rp319 but below the price [S0, S8]; blending the regime cases on the weights stated in the valuation section gives the probability-weighted target of Rp1,101 [S0]. The window runs from 31 October 2026 to 31 October 2027, so the MSCI Standalone decision — feedback by 30 April 2027, decision by 30 June 2027 — is inside it, as is the buyback end on 28 January 2027; the March 2027 float step does not bind TPIA [S5, S8, S9, S11, S13]. A half rather than 30.0% closure cuts the base regime target by roughly a quarter and does not restore the price [S0]; the return rests on the bull regime and on the premium not closing [S0].

Regulatory and index risk, high likelihood, medium impact. The OJK has raised the minimum free float with a first deadline in March 2027, and MSCI opened a Standalone consultation, feedback to April 2027 and a decision by mid-year; a further deletion would remove flow buyers from a thin register [S8, S9, S11].

Commodity and spread risk, high likelihood, high impact. The third quarter is the realised case: a spread collapse cut the gross margin to a thin level while revenue rose, operating EBITDA went negative, and only other gains rescued the attributable line [S17, S2]. The spread itself is the driver: if raw-material and manufacturing cost keeps outrunning revenue as it did in the third quarter, the thin margin persists, and this is why the bear is a spread case [S17, S2].

Macro and FX risk, medium likelihood, medium impact. Revenue is dollar-denominated and the shares rupiah-denominated; our macro desk has the rupiah under balance-of-payments pressure, a headwind, and a weaker rupiah raises the rupiah value of a dollar DCF but also imported costs [S0].

Operational risk, medium likelihood, high impact. A cracker or refinery outage is an earnings event, and the third quarter shows how little buffer the integrated site has; a Cycle & Carriage integration that fails to earn its cost of capital, or debt funding ahead of the 2027 maturities, would erode the deleveraging the base assumes [S5, S17, S18].

Liquidity and balance-sheet risk, medium likelihood, high impact. Heavy debt against cyclical EBITDA and a thin float make refinancing a flow event as much as a credit event [S17]. The current wall is covered by cash and current financial assets, but no covenant headroom is disclosed [S17, F80-F83]. The bear shows equity value going to zero on trough timing — a CA-EDC delay or a renewed downcycle [S0].

Governance and group risk, medium likelihood, medium impact. The controller owns most of the company and the group has multiple listed vehicles, so value can move between group vehicles rather than be earned in TPIA; the interim LK cannot show controlling-share pledges, so we flag a gap [S2, S17].
Signposts. A sustained spread recovery and an on-time CA-EDC start would make us more constructive; renewed oversupply or a Standalone decision, the reverse [S0, S9, S17].

Ownership and control. TPIA belongs to the Barito Pacific group of Prajogo Pangestu [S2]. Insider ownership is 74.5% and the free float 25.4%, above the minimum but concentrated enough that the controller sets the agenda and the price can sit away from fundamental value longer than the business cycle [S2, S0, S8].

The 2026 regime. The OJK rule raises the minimum free float, with a March 2027 first deadline and a delisting path [S8]. MSCI froze index increases, deletes HSC names, and opened the Standalone consultation on 15 October 2026 [S9]. TPIA was deleted from the Global Standard index in May 2026 but is not on the HSC list, so the deletion is an index-flow event, not a finding of wrongdoing; its float clears the March 2027 minimum [S11, S10, S8, S0].

Group transactions. Aster was acquired with Glencore, and Sembcorp has announced a planned stake in Aster Power, which explains the H1-2026 profit correction rather than a completed sale [S6]. Related-party trade is small: sales 1.9% of revenue, raw-material purchases 0.05% and finished-goods purchases 0.06%; the related-party note also discloses leases with group companies, a land-sale option and utility receivables, but no loan or guarantee to an affiliate is identified [S2, S17]. The cash-flow statement shows a US$21.4m loan to a related party in the nine months to September 2025 and none in the same period of 2026, so the related-party loan channel is currently dormant rather than a live leakage [S17]. The cited accounts and release name no counterparty for Cycle & Carriage, so we cannot rule out an affiliate seller [S17, S18]. The interim accounts are unaudited, and we have not sourced the latest auditor's opinion [S17]. ESG exposures are carbon intensity, process safety, and water and waste around the Cilegon estate [S5].

The next hard data are the fourth-quarter contribution from Cycle & Carriage, the FY2026 annual report and the CA-EDC start-up, scheduled for the first quarter of 2027 at 80.0% construction progress [S5, S18]. The buyback ends on 28 January 2027; executed volume against the Rp3,000 ceiling and IDR2.00tn fund tells us whether it is a bid or an authorisation [S13, S14]. The MSCI consultation closes at the end of April 2027, the largest regime catalyst [S9].

Between updates we watch gross margin, operating EBITDA, operating cash flow over EBITDA, net debt and interest cover, and the float against index news [S0, S8]. A placement or asset injection would change the count, flat today because the buyback is treasury-bound [S2, S13, S14].

bear.narrative: The third-quarter spread collapse persists: raw-material and manufacturing cost keeps outrunning revenue under a high Brent deck with only partial pass-through, so the gross margin stays near its third-quarter trough; the refinery runs at mid-cycle, CA-EDC start-up slips, and the enlarged debt load keeps interest cover thin.

bull.narrative: Petrochemical spreads widen from the third-quarter trough as the oil link normalises, the Singapore refinery captures a strong diesel and jet margin, CA-EDC starts on time into a protected domestic caustic and EDC market, and the balance sheet deleverages faster than assumed. Cycle & Carriage earns its cost of capital in the fourth quarter and beyond, adding the acquired automotive-distribution earnings that the base excludes as a wash. The shock is a realisation and spread shock, not a new-volume shock: capacity and capex are unchanged, so the bull does not compound revenue growth beyond what the asset base can produce, and the acquisition and CA-EDC Phase I earnings are treated as spread-neutral, not as a new revenue shock.

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +57.6% is the nine-month actual revenue of US$8,189.2m plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate of US$2,840.4m, giving US$11,029.6m on FY2025's US$7.0bn: the first full year of Aster Chemicals and Energy (ex-Shell Singapore refinery, acquired with Glencore) plus the Esso retail network from 1 Jan 2026 [S17, S5, S2]. FY2027E carries +5% rather than +3% because the US$800m CA-EDC chlor-alkali and EDC project, more than half complete and scheduled to start in Q1 2027, contributes a first full year of output and is already inside the capex path (FY2026E 6.9% of revenue, FY2027E 5.5%); from FY2028E we revert to +3% volume growth, not price [S5, S6, S17]. Phase II is disclosed at about US$1bn but remains at preparation stage with no final investment decision, so neither its capex nor its revenue is in the base; excluding a pre-FID project is the most likely treatment, not a zero valuation of Phase I, whose capex and first-year revenue are both modelled [S6].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Independent-observation midpoint, not the nine-month average. The base margin is set from two independent spread observations: H1-2026 earned 16.7% (revenue US$5,348.8m, cost US$4,455.5m) at Brent nearer US$84, and Q3-2026 alone earned 2.3% at roughly US$97-100, the actual trough [S17, S2, S0]. Grossed back through the calibrated oil link (60% of COGS exposed, four-fifths passed into prices, so 12% of COGS net) to the FY2025 anchor of US$68.1, H1 implies 19.0% and Q3 about 6.7%, a midpoint of about 12.9%; we set 13.4%, the top of that independent range because H1 is the only clean full half and Q3 is the cyclical trough [S17, S2, S0]. We no longer use the 16.0% 'nine-month trough': the nine-month average contains the clean H1 (nineteen-point revenue weight to H1 against eleven to Q3), so the two brackets overlap and 16.0% is not an independent lower bound [S17, S2]. FY2026E is rebuilt from the nine-month actual gross profit of US$959.9m (revenue US$8,189.2m less raw materials and manufacturing US$7,229.3m) plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's 2.3% on the US$2,840.4m run-rate, giving 9.1% at the deck's US$96 Brent; 13.4% at the anchor reproduces that through the link [S17, S2, S0]. There is no sourced evidence of a fourth-quarter spread recovery, spot Brent is US$112.79 and the pass-through lag squeezes spreads further, so holding the Q3 run-rate for Q4 is the most likely path, not a cautious one [S2, S0]. The inventory allowance is unchanged at US$62.623m across both period columns (Note 8), so the third-quarter collapse is spread, not a write-down [S17]. At the deck's Brent path the effective margin runs about 9.1% in FY2026E, 11.0% in FY2027E and 11.0% at the terminal Brent; no public Asian petrochemical spread index exists in our archive, so the cost-curve quartile remains a judgment (mid-curve) [S17, S0]. The sensitivity grid shows plus or minus two points.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Calibration, not a company disclosure: we set 60% of COGS as oil-linked because naphtha and refinery crude dominate raw materials while utilities, labour and fixed manufacturing cost do not move with Brent [S2]. The pair split/pass is fitted on the only clean consolidated half, H1-2026, and tested against the FY2025 and H1-2025 comparatives below, which are scope-broken because Aster consolidated only from mid-2025 [S2].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Calibration, not a company disclosure: with the 60% cost share, 80% pass-through gives a net 12% of COGS exposed to the Brent move, which is the pair that reproduces the 16.7% H1-2026 gross margin at that half's Brent and the 19.1% base margin at the FY2025 anchor [S2]. The H1-2026 half is the only clean scope; FY2025 and H1-2025 margins are distorted by the mid-2025 Aster consolidation and therefore cannot validate the pair [S2, S0].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Full reconciliation to the H1-2026 LK lines: selling 41.554 + G&A 91.346 + final tax 3.286 + other net loss 39.101 + depreciation 164.131 = US$339.418m on revenue of US$5,348.769m, which is 6.35% [S2]. The prior 6.2% omitted part of the other net loss; the ratio is restated to the full build. Depreciation sits below the gross-profit line in this LK, so it is included here and added back to EBITDA. The other net loss is kept as recurring because the note does not identify it as one-off; excluding it would lower the ratio to 5.6% and raise value, so it is a disclosed conservatism, not a hidden one [S2].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: H1-2026 depreciation of US$164.1m on US$5,348.8m revenue (3.07%); the pack's FY2025 D&A is close to the LK run-rate, so no restatement is needed [S2, S0].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Nine-month acquisitions of PP&E were US$572.5m (6.99% of nine-month revenue), running the US$800m CA-EDC project and sustaining the refinery and cracker, above the H1 run-rate of 5.3%; FY2026E is set at that 6.9% and then steps down to 5.5% in FY2027E and 4% once CA-EDC completes, converging on D&A plus growth [S17, S2, S5]. CA-EDC Phase II, which management says is at the preparation stage at a similar size, is disclosed but excluded from the capex path until a final investment decision; including it would add capex without adding the revenue it is meant to earn, so the base carries Phase I only and the report flags the omission [S6].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The 30 September actual is a released ratio, not a normal one: trade receivables of US$1,005.7m (US$985.5m third parties plus US$20.1m related parties) plus inventories of US$1,761.3m less trade payables of US$1,685.5m equals US$1,081.4m, 9.9% of annualised nine-month revenue of US$10,918.9m [S17, F71, F72, F70]. Inventories fell US$476.7m in the nine months (2,237.9 to 1,761.3) while revenue rose, and 9M operating cash flow of US$378.9m is therefore negative before that release; capitalising the released ratio to perpetuity would assume the group never rebuilds the inventory it sold [S17, S2]. H1-2026, before the release, was 12.8% (receivables US$844m plus inventories US$2,238m less payables US$1,710m), and that is our normalised path from FY2027E: FY2026E stays at the 30 September actual, FY2027E rebuilds to 12.8% and holds it [S17, S2]. The rebuild is a one-year working-capital outflow in FY2027E, after which the ratio is stable.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Recalibrated to the nine-month note, not the half. Note 38 shows nine-month current tax of US$12.514m and a deferred expense of US$1.634m, total US$14.148m on PBT of US$409.074m, a 3.5% effective rate; the half-year's 14.5% was inflated by a Q3 deferred-tax reversal, so the reviewer is right that 14.5% overstates the forward charge [S17]. The low current charge follows a US$250.207m current-year fiscal loss at the parent and the tax-facility benefit of US$65.626m, while subsidiaries carry the final tax that cannot be offset [S17]. We start FY2026E at the 3.5% actual and step up to 18% by FY2030E, below the 22% statutory rate because final tax on revenue and the facility benefit persist; the ramp reflects the finite stock of fiscal losses being consumed, and is the reason value is higher than the prior build [S17, S2].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Nine-month finance costs of US$306.3m annualise to US$408.3m against the 30 Sep 2026 financing liabilities of US$6,093.9m, a 6.7% average cash cost including the refinery acquisition facilities; we use 6.9% on the opening forecast debt to reflect the run-rate after the Q3 drawdown [S17, S2].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Recalibrated to the LK's cash and cash equivalents: nine-month finance income of US$104.2m annualises to US$139.0m on the 30 Sep 2026 cash of US$2,962.7m, a 4.7% yield; we carry 5% on opening cash [S17, S2].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: FY2026E only: the LK's financing-liabilities reconciliation shows the total rising from US$5,414.2m at 1 January 2026 to US$6,093.9m at 30 September 2026, so the forecast carries the US$679.6m nine-month drawdown; the 30 Sep debt is the opening run-rate. Thereafter no new net debt: operating EBITDA and capex broadly fund interest and the small dividend [S17, S2, S6, S7].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: the US$1.77bn Aster bargain-purchase gain in H1-2025 and the Sembcorp-related corrections are one-offs and are excluded from the forecast, though they remain in reported history [S2, S6].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Nine-month profit attributable to non-controlling interests was US$115.1m of US$394.9m (29.1%), above the H1 23.7%, driven by the 40% CDIA minority and the Glencore/Sembcorp interests in the Aster complex, whose share rises when the operating result is weak; we carry 28% [S17, S2].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The group paid US$30m of parent dividends in H1-2026 and US$50m in FY2025; the 10% payout reflects the modest DPS on the enlarged share count rather than a stated policy ratio [S2, S0].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Held flat. The new programme, disclosed on 29 October 2026, runs to 28 January 2027 for up to Rp2tn, 1.6bn shares (1.84% of issued) at a maximum of Rp3,000 a share, after the 19 October programme (Rp1tn, up to 0.92%) was terminated on 28 October 2026 [S13, S14, S12]. We still do not shrink the count: the shares are bought into treasury (an asset, not a cancelled share), execution is discretionary and undisclosed to date, and the engine carries no buyback cash-out line, so a count cut without its cash cost would overstate equity value; at the market price the repurchase is close to value-neutral against our fundamental value, while the Rp3,000 ceiling sits well above it, which we read as group intent to support the price rather than as a valuation input [S14, S0].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: US-dollar reporting: 2.5% nominal terminal growth, in line with long-run chemical volume growth plus dollar inflation, and below the Indonesian CPI deck because revenue is dollar-denominated [S5].

challenges.challenge: The base margin is not the midpoint it claims. The 'nine-month trough' (16.0% at the US$68.1 anchor) is the 9M average, which contains the clean H1 (19.0% at the anchor); the two brackets overlap and are not independent. The actual trough observation is Q3 alone: 2.3% gross on US$2,840m revenue at roughly US$97-100 Brent, which grosses back to only about 6-7% at the anchor. On the independent pair (H1 16.7% at ~US$84 vs Q3 2.3%) the midpoint is ~12-13% at the anchor, not 17.5%. The model's own FY2026E gross profit of US$1,483m less the 9M actual US$960m implies Q4 gross profit of ~US$523m on ~US$2,843m revenue — an 18.4% Q4 margin, above the clean H1, one quarter after the 2.3% print and into rising spot Brent. The engine's sensitivity shows a 2pp lower gross margin takes the 12-month value to Rp869; 1.5pp lower (the 9M-implied 16.0%) takes it to ~Rp965 and the lens target to ~Rp1,060, below the Rp1,350 price. The base is therefore not the most probable path and the uplift is unsourced.
challenges.answer: FATAL accepted. Base gross margin rebuilt to 13.4% at the FY2025 anchor from the independent observations (H1 19.0%, Q3 6.7% grossed back) rather than the overlapping 9M average; FY2026E rebuilt from 9M gross profit of US$959.9m plus Q4 at the Q3 2.3% run-rate, giving 9.1% on the deck path. DCF equity floors at zero, rating ADD to REDUCE, target Rp1,493 to Rp1,098.

challenges.challenge: The ADD does not survive the desk's doubled-bear test. The 12-month fundamental is Rp1,360, only 0.7% above the Rp1,350 price, and the summary calls it 'still below' the price — the opposite. The base business scenario is Rp1,276, below price; the probability-weighted value is lifted above water by the 25% bull at Rp2,888, which contributes more expected value (about Rp722m) than the 50% base (about Rp638m). With bear at 50% (base 25%, bull 25%) the fundamental is Rp1,041 and the lens target about Rp1,143, a -15% return. §5 labels commodity and spread risk 'high likelihood' but assigns the bear 25%.
challenges.answer: Corrected 'still below' to 'above'. On the corrected base the DCF floors at zero, the base business case is zero and the base regime target Rp959 is below the price, so the doubled-bear test fails and the rating falls to REDUCE. Scenario weights moved to bear 0.35, base 0.45, bull 0.20 to reconcile the high-likelihood spread risk with the bear weight.

challenges.challenge: The MSCI Standalone decision is inside, not outside, the 12-month window: from 31 October 2026 the horizon runs to 31 October 2027 and the decision is due by 30 June 2027 (feedback to 30 April 2027). §5 says 'the MSCI decision falls after the window', while §4 uses the same decision to cap re-rating as the base keeps 70% of the premium. With the regulator's largest regime catalyst inside the window and the May 2026 deletion already having removed index buyers, the 30% base closure (compress_base) has no TPIA-specific support; the buyback support ends 28 January 2027, leaving about nine months unsupported.
challenges.answer: Window corrected: 31 Oct 2026 to 31 Oct 2027, so the MSCI decision by 30 Jun 2027 (feedback 30 Apr 2027) is inside it. Re-argued compress_base with the decision inside and the buyback ending 28 Jan 2027; re-tested a half closure, which takes the base regime target to about Rp697 and the weighted target down with it, so a higher closure does not restore the price.

challenges.challenge: The commodity-card output contract requires NAV at the through-cycle price and at spot. The report gives Rp1,112 on the deck path, says the anchor value is 'higher' and the spot value is 'zero', but neither is quantified. Worse, the deck path never reaches the stated US$75 anchor (terminal Brent ~84.5), so the DCF is not struck at the through-cycle price, and the base-input margin is anchored to FY2025's US$68.1 — below the US$75 marker. The card's primary output, the through-cycle NAV, is missing.
challenges.answer: Stated that the deck path ends below the US$75 anchor and the DCF is struck on the market path, not the anchor; that the engine discounts one Brent path and cannot be struck flat at the anchor; the calibrated link (~0.1pp margin per dollar) means the anchor value is above the deck-path DCF; at spot with no reversion value is zero. Stated the price uses a higher anchor than ours. Full flat-anchor re-strike is flagged as a method limitation, not claimed.

challenges.challenge: Cycle & Carriage completed on 15 October 2026 and management guides group revenue toward US$15bn, but the base carries no acquired revenue or earnings and the bull narrative never mentions it; CA-EDC Phase I's own contribution is also not isolated beyond the generic +5% FY2027 growth. Excluding both the consideration and the earnings is a wash only if the price paid equals value, and the report assumes that without saying so. The bull at Rp2,888 therefore omits the acquisition management says adds about US$4bn of annual revenue.
challenges.answer: Cycle & Carriage is now an explicit wash (consideration assumed equal to acquired earnings) in the base, with a positive contribution in the bull narrative on management's revenue guidance. CA-EDC Phase I is isolated: the FY2027E 5% growth step versus the 3% baseline is its first full year, and the acquisition is outside the growth path.

challenges.challenge: There is no funding or dilution assessment. The base assumes refinancing and no new net debt after FY2026 while CA-EDC Phase II (~US$1bn), the undisclosed C&C consideration and the 2027 maturities lie ahead. A rights issue or private placement is the modal konglo capital-markets act and would dilute per-share value; §7 says only that 'a placement or asset injection would change the count'. The konglo card requires a check for a rights issue or placement in preparation.
challenges.answer: Added a funding and dilution assessment: no rights issue, placement or standby facility disclosed in the archived filings and press for C&C, CA-EDC Phase II or the 2027 maturities; the current wall is covered about three times by cash; a placement is low-to-moderate probability with a proportionate per-share cost. Numeric arithmetic sits in post_bs_review, prose stays number-free.

challenges.challenge: C&C's seller is not identified in the cited sources. S17 (Note 1/2 subsequent events, page 169) records only the CSPA date (21 August 2026) and the business acquired; S18 records the 15 October completion and the Mercedes-Benz partnership, not the counterparty. The claim 'bought from an external seller, not a group affiliate' is therefore unsourced, and it is the basis for saying C&C adds no related-party flow — on a konglo name where asset injections inside the group are the modal value-destruction channel. Note 42's loans and guarantees to affiliates are not reviewed, only trade.
challenges.answer: Deleted the unsourced 'external seller' claim. §6 now states the cited accounts and release name no counterparty, so an affiliate seller cannot be ruled out and the acquisition is not treated as free of related-party flow; the LK related-party note discloses trade balances and its loans and guarantees to affiliates are flagged as not reviewed.

challenges.challenge: The multiple cross-check is not reconciled. 'At the peer median the EV/EBITDA check is close to the DCF': the computed peer median is 5.93x; on FY2026E EBITDA of US$1,121m that gives equity of about US$3.19bn, Rp669 a share, 40% below the Rp1,112 DCF. Only FY2027E EBITDA at 5.93x approaches it (about Rp990, still 11% below). The report does not say which year, and the divergence is unexplained. At the 8.14x peer-median PE the FY2027E check is about Rp857.
challenges.answer: Removed 'close': §4 now states the peer-median EV/EBITDA check is far below the DCF on FY2026E (near-zero Q4 EBITDA) and closer but still below on FY2027E, and the PE check is below on both because earnings are small and depreciated; the peer table shows both years at the median.

challenges.challenge: Two placeholder unit errors misstate key konglo statements. (1) §5: 'The base carries 0.5% of the probability' — the model probability is 0.5, i.e. 50%; val.scenarios.base.prob passed to pctv treats a fraction as a percent. (2) §4: the buyback is 'large against average daily value of IDR395,145,892.54tn' — the datapack ADTV is IDR395,145,892,539, i.e. Rp0.40tn, so the formatter is 1,000 times too high and the sentence contradicts 'large against'. Both sit in the flow argument that supports the lens.
challenges.answer: Fixed both formatters: scenario probabilities now render with pct0 (0.45 reads 45%) and the datapack ADTV now uses idrb (Rp0.395tn, not Rp395tn). Audited the pctv uses in §4 and §5; the buyback sentence and the probability table now agree.

challenges.challenge: The buyback cash out is excluded while the count is held flat. Up to Rp2.00tn (about US$110m) could leave the balance sheet by 28 January 2027; the model carries neither the cash out nor any treasury accretion, and the post_bs_review states the engine carries neither. Excluding both sides is neutral only at fundamental value; at Rp1,350 (1.14 times today's fundamental) execution transfers value from continuing holders, and if the buyback is what supports the premium the lens keeps, the interaction is not modelled.
challenges.answer: Explained rather than modelled: the engine carries neither the cash out nor the treasury accretion, and above fundamental value that combination overstates per-share value if the programme is fully executed, so the error runs against our REDUCE. Discretionary, undisclosed execution is why we state the direction rather than model a volume.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 (The cross-checks, reconciled) is stale after the FATAL C1 revision: it says the peer-median EV/EBITDA check is 'far below the DCF' on FY2026E and 'still sits below it' on FY2027E, but the DCF now floors at zero and the twelve-month fundamental is Rp319. At the 5.93x peer median the FY2027E check is about Rp408, above the fundamental, and the FY2026E check about Rp103; the PE check is about Rp85 and Rp272. The sentence reverses the FY2027E direction and does not reconcile the checks against the fundamental or the Rp1,350 price. QC flagged this FIX as Q7 and it is unchanged.
challenges.answer: Rewrote Section 4's cross-check paragraph against the corrected model: at the peer median the FY2026E EV/EBITDA check implies about a third of the twelve-month fundamental, and the FY2027E check is a genuine counter-signal about a quarter above it, because the multiple capitalises pre-D&A EBITDA while FY2027E FCFF is still negative after capex and working capital; the PE check is below the fundamental on both years and neither approaches the price. The stale 'far below the DCF / still below' claim is deleted. Rating and target are unchanged because the multiple weight is zero. The checks are stated relative to the fundamental (about a third; about a quarter above) because report prose carries no typed figures; the peer median is shown in the peer table [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 5 (Commodity and spread risk) attributes the bear case to 'Renewed Chinese capacity' and cites [S0, S17]; neither the data pack nor the nine-month LK supports a Chinese capacity addition, and the same unsourced driver is in the bear narrative in fund record. The claim is presented as fact without a public source and is the causal narrative for the high-likelihood spread risk on a cyclicals name. QC flagged this FIX as Q8 and it is unchanged.
challenges.answer: Replaced the unsourced Chinese-capacity driver in Section 5 and in the bear narrative with the realised, sourced driver: the third-quarter spread collapse, where raw-material and manufacturing cost outran revenue and the thin margin persisted. Removed the 'supply-driven' claim from Section 2 and softened the bull narrative's 'older Asian crackers shut' clause for the same reason. No capacity-addition claim remains on S0/S17 [S17, S2].

challenges.challenge: Section 6 says the LK related-party loans and guarantees to affiliates were 'not reviewed'. That defers MATERIAL red-team challenge C7, which required the Note 42 position. QC Q9 records that the archived S17 Note 42 discloses related-party trade, leases, land and options, and the cash-flow statement shows a US$21.4m loan to a related party in 9M-2025 and nil in 9M-2026, with no affiliate guarantee line identified. On a Barito konglo name the related-party channel is the modal value-destruction route, so leaving it unreviewed is not an answer on substance.
challenges.answer: Reviewed the related-party note and the cash-flow statement on substance: the note discloses leases with group companies, a land-sale option, utility receivables and small trade flows, but identifies no loan or guarantee to an affiliate; the cash-flow statement shows a US$21.4m related-party loan payment in 9M-2025 and nil in 9M-2026, so the loan channel is dormant rather than a live leakage. Added fact F100 and removed the 'not reviewed' gap [S17, F100].

missing_bull_case.note: No quantified NAV at the US$75 long-run Brent anchor or at spot, contrary to the commodity card's output contract; the anchor value is only 'higher' than Rp1,112. The completed Cycle & Carriage acquisition and CA-EDC Phase I's own contribution earn no value in the base or the bull, so management's ~US$15bn group-revenue ambition is unmodelled.

missing_bear_case.note: The MSCI Standalone decision (feedback to Apr 2027, decision by end-Jun 2027) is inside the 12-month window, but §5 says it falls after; the base keeps 70% of the premium partly on that error. No funding/dilution assessment for CA-EDC Phase II (~US$1bn), the undisclosed C&C consideration and the 2027 maturities; a rights issue/placement is the modal konglo act. 'Renewed Chinese capacity' is unsourced.

assumption_realism.note: The 17.5% base-input margin is above the 16.0% implied by the 9M actual and treats the 9M average (which contains the clean H1) as the trough, omitting Q3's 2.3%. FY2026E 13.4% gross implies an 18.4% Q4 margin on Q3 revenue run-rate into rising spot Brent. The margin anchor is FY2025's US$68.1 Brent, not the US$75 through-cycle anchor.

evidence_and_citations.note: Nine-month, buyback, tax, Esso, Sembcorp and C&C facts verify against S17/S18/S6 and the facts lint passes. But 'C&C was bought from an external seller, not a group affiliate' is unsupported: S17 and S18 name no seller. CDIA is marked at Rp119.652928 while its current model fundamental is Rp120.044. Two placeholder unit errors are recorded in C9.

valuation_method_fit.note: A 100% FCFF DCF is correct for the industry and the bridge (associates added, minorities deducted, CDIA at fundamental) is coherent. But the through-cycle NAV at the anchor is unquantified, and 'at the peer median the EV/EBITDA check is close to the DCF' holds only for FY2027E (Rp990, 11% below); at FY2026E it is Rp669, 40% below.

bias_and_tone.note: The summary says the probability-weighted fundamental Rp1,360 is 'still below' the Rp1,350 price — it is above (a v4 leftover). The base business scenario Rp1,276 is below price and the positive expected value leans on the 25% bull (Rp2,888). Set bear to 50% and the lens target is ~Rp1,143, below price. §5 calls spread risk 'high likelihood' yet gives the bear 25%.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The Brent path (96, 84, 80, 78, 76.5, then 84.46 by FY2035E) never reaches the stated US$75 anchor, so the DCF terminal is struck above the through-cycle marker; the margin is anchored to FY2025's US$68.1. The cost link is applied consistently across years, but the anchor is asserted, not used.

conservatism_audit.note: Disclosed conservatisms are real and mostly sourced: capex 4% vs D&A 3.1% in perpetuity, the H1 other-net loss kept recurring, NWC rebuilt to 12.8%, tax ramp to 15-18%. The offsetting optimism is the margin (above actuals), the 100% mark on US$300m of FVTPL/credit-linked financial assets after removing the prior haircut, and excluding the buyback cash out while holding the count flat.

calibration.note: The FY2025A to FY2026E BLOCK gate is justified with a transition source (Aster consolidated from mid-2025). But FY+1 at the last actual (9M-2026 at ~US$97 Brent) does not reproduce: model FY2026E gross margin 13.4% vs 11.7% actual, and the implied Q4 is 18.4%; the upward drift is not sourced.

signoff.notes: Approved on the merits. The three prior concerns are resolved on substance: L1 — Section 4 now states the peer-median FY2026E EV/EBITDA check implies about a third of the twelve-month fundamental and the FY2027E check about a quarter above it, the correct direction; L2 — the unsourced "renewed Chinese capacity" driver is gone from Section 5 and the bear narrative, replaced by the realised Q3 spread collapse [S17, S2]; L3 — Section 6 reviews Note 42 on substance (trade 1.9% / 0.05% / 0.06%, leases, land and utility balances, no affiliate loan or guarantee identified; US$21.4m 9M-2025 related-party loan flow, nil in 9M-2026) with fact F100. QC round 2 passed with 0 BLOCK and the Q13 FIX is implemented and reads correctly: Section 5 puts the base-regime target at Rp964 (30.0% log-gap closure) and the probability-weighted target at Rp1,101, matching Section 4 and the engine. FATAL C1 and MATERIAL C2-C10 are answered. The call holds against its own evidence: the base DCF floors at zero, the twelve-month fundamental is Rp319, the Rp1,350 price is 4.86x it, and even retaining 78% of the log premium (3.454x) the target is Rp1,101, a -18.4% return; the anchor re-strike (about 1pp higher margin, just over Rp300 a share) cannot restore the price. The konglo lens is explained in Sections 4-6; CDIA is marked at its own lens fundamental of Rp120.044, consistent with the CDIA model (price Rp362, target about Rp287), so the group marks agree. Single-name batch: no cross-name or shared-input tilt. Consensus quarantine clean — no broker rating, target or consensus met; sources are filings, company releases, index/regulator material and the S0 data pack. Lint PASS (warnings: 3,524 words against the 3,500 update range; one valuation method, justified by the trailing-pack multiples). Journal for the Director: the BRPT SOTP still carries TPIA at its pre-revision fundamental Rp1,346.88 and target Rp1,489.55 against TPIA v7 Rp319 and Rp1,101 — refresh the BRPT TPIA mark before BRPT publishes (outside this batch). Non-material notes: Section 3 prose calls the 13.4% margin the "top" of the independent H1/Q3 range where the assumptions basis and the arithmetic make it the midpoint; the Q14 "land-sale option" wording against the completed PPJB sale; minority_pct 28% against the 29.1% actual (Q15) is immaterial to the FCFF DCF.

bias.note: The REDUCE rests on the 4.86x price/fundamental premium, not on an understated base. The base-input gross margin of 13.4% is the top of the independent H1-2026/Q3-2026 range (midpoint about 12.9%), the US$300m financial-assets bridge is marked at 100% of fair value after removing the prior haircut, the minority profit share is 28% against a 29.1% nine-month actual, and the konglo base keeps 70% of the log premium with no regime flags - all mild optimism. Disclosed conservatisms (capex 4% vs D&A 3.1%, NWC rebuild to 12.8%, tax ramp to 18%, recurring other-net loss, Q4 held at the Q3 trough, C&C wash excluding acquired earnings) are sourced. The business DCF equity is only -US$71.8m before the floor and the 12-month fundamental of Rp318.7 is entirely the 20% bull, so the call is not a stacked bear; the doubled-bear re-weight still puts the target below the price. No consensus or broker material found.

recomputed.item: CDIA minority add-back vs US$473.866m book

findings.finding: Section 5 ('The konglo lens, stated plainly') says the base regime closes 30% of the log premium and keeps the rest 'putting the target at Rp1,101'. The base regime target is Rp964 (Section 4 and the engine agree); Rp1,101 is the 25/50/25 probability-weighted target. The next sentence then treats the base regime target as one that a half closure cuts by roughly a quarter, contradicting the Rp1,101 attribution.
findings.answer: Section 5 now puts the base-regime target at val.konglo.scenarios.base.tp and describes val.tp_final as the probability-weighted blend of the regime cases on the weights stated in Section 4, so Sections 4 and 5 agree. No model input, assumption, fact, rating or target changed.

findings.finding: Section 6 says the related-party note discloses 'a land-sale option'. S17 Note 42 (p.159) has a completed related-party land sale-and-purchase (PPJB No.6 with CAA and CCP, US$26.223m in FY2025) and, separately, a CDI option to buy 51% of CPN's paid-up shares; calling the land item an option conflates the two. The Q9 substance is verified: nil 9M-2026 related-party loan flow, US$21.441m in 9M-2025 (F100), no affiliate guarantee identified.

The model carries minority_pct at 28% while the nine-month actual is 29.1% (US$115.1m of US$394.9m); the basis states the actual but gives no reason for 28%. The gap is slightly optimistic for parent earnings but immaterial to the FCFF DCF, which floors at zero.

Prior QC FIX items Q7-Q9 are verified resolved in version 7: Section 4 puts the peer-median FY2026E EV/EBITDA check at about a third of fundamental and FY2027E about a quarter above, deleting the direction reversal [S0]; Section 5 and the bear narrative replace 'renewed Chinese capacity' with the realised Q3 spread collapse [S17, S2]; Section 6 reviews Note 42 and the cash-flow loan line, with F100 recording the US$21.441m 9M-2025 related-party loan and nil 9M-2026 [S17, F100].

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves +11.4pp from FY2025A: source the change
